- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00) in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 1.00) in the recent history, model often overestimates upward momentum; reduce forecast peak values to prevent overshoot.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days), especially after recent price drops — apply upward bias to early forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days), model tends to overreact and forecast a prolonged high — reduce forecast slope after spike to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model often fails to adjust quickly — apply a lagged correction: delay upward/downward shift by 1–2 days in forecast.
- Model tends to underestimate true price in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon — apply slight upward bias to end of forecast to account for momentum or policy effects.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often drifts toward mean — apply slight upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
